papers.title: Complete Mitochondrial Genome of a French Bulldog with Carcinoma planoepitheliale keratodes G1: A Descriptive Case Report.
papers.abstract: French Bulldogs, like other brachycephalic breeds, are predisposed to a variety of genetic and tumour-related disorders. While mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) mutations have been documented in canine tumours, no prior study has examined the entire mitochondrial genome in this breed. In this study, we analysed mtDNA obtained from blood and tumour tissue of a 10-year-old male French Bulldog diagnosed with carcinoma planoepitheliale keratodes (G1). Complete sequencing and comparative bioinformatic analysis revealed 22 sequence variants, including nine in protein-coding genes, two in RNA-coding genes, t
papers.summary: This case report sequences the complete mitochondrial genome from blood and tumor tissue of a single French Bulldog with a grade 1 squamous cell carcinoma, identifying 22 sequence variants including nine in protein-coding genes. The work is purely descriptive, with no functional validation or comparison to a reference population, so it establishes a baseline observation rather than a causal link between mtDNA variants and cancer.

papers.title: Machine learning and computational approaches to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) remains one of the most lethal cancers affecting children, adolescents and young adults and is near-universally resistant to treatment. Histone H3-alterations establish a profoundly dysregulated epigenetic landscape that promotes extensive intratumoral heterogeneity and cellular plasticity, key drivers of therapeutic resistance and treatment failure. Although single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the study of tumor evolution, the mechanisms underpinning treatment resistance in DMG remain poorly understood. This Review examines how
papers.summary: This review examines how machine learning and computational approaches can be used to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma (DMG), a lethal pediatric brain cancer driven by histone H3 alterations that create epigenetic dysregulation and intratumoral heterogeneity. It highlights how single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, combined with computational modeling, could help uncover mechanisms of treatment resistance that remain poorly understood.

papers.title: KmerSignificance score: A discriminative and biologically informed framework for viral k-mer prioritization.
papers.abstract: Distinguishing closely related viral strains requires identifying genomic regions where subtle sequence differences carry biological significance. While k-mer-based approaches offer computational efficiency for genome analysis, existing methods lack standardized frameworks for evaluating which k-mers are most informative. Current selection strategies focus primarily on statistical discriminative power without integrating biological context. We introduce KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a k-mer prioritization framework combining three components: an information-theoretic method measuring strain-di
papers.summary: The authors introduce KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a framework for prioritizing k-mers that combines statistical discriminative power with biological context to better distinguish closely related viral strains. KSS integrates an information-theoretic measure of strain discrimination with additional biologically informed components, addressing the gap in standardized k-mer selection methods. This provides a more interpretable and biologically relevant approach to viral genome analysis.

papers.title: An Integrated Framework Coupling Hierarchical Hyperspectral i-trait Screening, Gene Identification, and Functional Validation for Genetic Dissection of Salt Tolerance in Cotton.
papers.abstract: Cotton is an economically pivotal fiber crop worldwide, but its growth and yield are critically limited by soil salinity. Salt tolerance is a complex quantitative trait, and conventional destructive phenotyping methods have long hindered the efficiency and accuracy of gene discovery and genetic dissection. To overcome this phenotyping bottleneck and establish a streamlined workflow from phenotype to gene, we developed an integrated framework coupling dynamic hyperspectral phenomics, hierarchical trait selection, genome-wide association study (GWAS), and functional validation, and applied it to
papers.summary: This study develops an integrated framework that combines dynamic hyperspectral imaging, hierarchical trait selection, GWAS, and functional validation to dissect salt tolerance in cotton. The approach overcomes the limitations of destructive phenotyping by enabling non-invasive, high-throughput screening of salt tolerance traits, leading to the identification and validation of candidate genes. This provides a streamlined workflow from phenotype to gene for complex quantitative traits.

papers.title: [Genome-wide identification, expression profiling, and natural allelic variation analysis of the ckx genes in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor)].
papers.abstract: Cytokinin (CK) is one of the essential plant hormones, and cytokinin oxidase (CKX) is the key enzyme for CK degradation. Currently, the ckx gene family of rice (Oryza sativa) and maize (Zea mays) have been characterized, while a genome-wide analysis of the ckx gene family in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) has not been reported. This study aims to identify the Sbckx gene family in sorghum, analyze its evolutionary characteristics and expression patterns, and screen for key genes. A combined approach of bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation was utilized to examine sorghum subjected to a
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study performs the first genome-wide identification and characterization of the cytokinin oxidase (ckx) gene family in sorghum, analyzing their evolutionary relationships and expression patterns. The authors also screen for natural allelic variation in these genes, identifying key Sbckx genes that may be targeted for crop improvement.

papers.title: A Practical Guide to Dereplication in Natural Products Metabolomics.
papers.abstract: Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)-based metabolomics has become a central approach for characterizing the chemical diversity of biological systems, particularly in natural product discovery. However, the scale and complexity of untargeted LC-MS/MS datasets present a persistent challenge: only a small fraction of detected features can be confidently assigned to known structures, leaving much of the metabolome unexplored. Dereplication and annotation tools have rapidly expanded to address this bottleneck, including molecular networking, spectral library matching, substruc
papers.summary: This paper provides a practical guide to dereplication strategies for LC-MS/MS-based natural products metabolomics, addressing the bottleneck that most detected features cannot be confidently assigned to known structures. It surveys and explains annotation tools including molecular networking, spectral library matching, and substructure prediction, offering guidance on how to apply them to untargeted datasets.

papers.title: Phylogeographical structure and genetic introgression in Salmonella enterica serotype Napoli: a genomic epidemiology study.
papers.abstract: Salmonella enterica serotype Napoli (S Napoli), a non-typhoidal Salmonella serotype that has been emerging in Italy, Switzerland, and France since the mid-1990s, has an unusual epidemiological profile that suggests a role for the environment in the transmission of these bacteria. The genomics of S Napoli has been inadequately characterised; we, therefore, aimed to provide a robust genomic framework for S Napoli surveillance.
papers.summary: This genomic epidemiology study characterizes the phylogeographic structure and genetic introgression of Salmonella enterica serotype Napoli, an emerging non-typhoidal serotype in Italy, Switzerland, and France since the mid-1990s. The authors provide a robust genomic framework for surveillance of this pathogen, revealing unusual environmental transmission patterns.

papers.title: Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.
papers.abstract: As domestic and international travel has expanded, the risk of the cross-border dissemination of infectious pathogens has increased, as clearly evidenced during the COVID-19 pandemic. Aircraft- and airport-based wastewater surveillance can provide timely, aggregate evidence of pathogen circulation among mobile populations and may complement clinical, genomic, and syndromic surveillance at points of entry. The strongest evidence for this approach comes from SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection and variant monitoring in aircraft lavatory wastewater, airport terminal wastewater, and airport-associated wastew
papers.summary: This perspective argues that aircraft and airport wastewater surveillance can offer timely, aggregated evidence of pathogen circulation among travelers, complementing clinical and genomic surveillance at points of entry. The strongest evidence comes from SARS-CoV-2 RNA and variant detection in lavatory and terminal wastewater, but the authors stress that a sustainable, integrated approach is needed to realize its public health potential.

papers.title: Ultrafast Workflow for Accurate Full-length ABO Genotyping using Nanopore Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Rapid ABO discrepancy resolution is critical for transfusion safety. However, current short-read sequencing cannot resolve phase across the 21.9 kb ABO gene. Here, the aim is to developed a nanopore-based workflow for full-length ABO genotyping. A workflow combining a long-range PCR (LR-PCR) amplicon spanning the ABO gene was generated from genomic DNA from 63 serologically discrepant donors and sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) Platform. PacBio HiFi sequencing was used as an orthogonal reference standard. Variant calling and haplotype reconstruction were performed using a uni
papers.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
papers.summary: This study presents a nanopore-based workflow for full-length ABO genotyping that uses long-range PCR to amplify the entire 21.9 kb ABO gene, followed by Oxford Nanopore sequencing and haplotype reconstruction. Tested on 63 serologically discrepant donor samples with PacBio HiFi as an orthogonal reference, the method resolves phased variants across the full gene, overcoming the limitation of short-read sequencing in this highly homologous region. The workflow enables rapid resolution of ABO typing discrepancies for transfusion safety.

papers.title: Genomic insights into non-tuberculous mycobacteria isolated from patients in a Chinese hospital.
papers.abstract: Non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are increasingly recognized as important opportunistic pathogens, yet the genomic basis of their antimicrobial resistance and virulence in clinical settings remains incompletely understood. We performed whole-genome sequencing on 28 clinical isolates of NTM collected from Chinese patients (primarily bronchoalveolar lavage fluid) between 2022 and 2025, combined with broth microdilution susceptibility testing and comprehensive bioinformatics analysis. The collection comprised diverse species, including Mycobacterium intracellulare, Mycobacterium chimaera, Mycob
papers.summary: This study sequenced the genomes of 28 non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) clinical isolates from Chinese patients and combined this with antimicrobial susceptibility testing to explore the genetic basis of resistance and virulence. The collection spanned multiple species, including M. intracellulare and M. chimaera, providing a genomic snapshot of clinically relevant NTM diversity. The work contributes to understanding how specific genetic features may underlie drug resistance and pathogenicity in these emerging opportunistic pathogens.

papers.title: XenoMix: Estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation microarrays enable cost-effective, high-throughput profiling of human and mouse samples and are widely used to study epigenetic alterations in cancer. Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models complement this approach by preserving primary tumor characteristics while enabling in vivo studies of drug response and therapy resistance. However, it remains difficult to quantify mouse DNA contamination in PDX DNA methylation data generated using microarrays. We present XenoMix, a light-weight computational tool for quantifying mouse DNA contamination directly from DNA methylation data i
papers.summary: XenoMix is a lightweight computational tool that estimates the proportion of mouse DNA contamination in Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) DNA methylation microarray data. It addresses the common problem of mixed human-mouse signal in PDX epigenomic profiling, enabling researchers to quantify and account for contamination without additional experimental steps.

papers.title: Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture, making it a powerful approach for studying plant developmental transitions. However, preparing small and structurally complex plant tissues for spatial transcriptomics remains technically challenging because samples must be rapidly preserved, precisely oriented, serially sectioned, and accurately positioned within the limited capture area of the Visium slides. Here, we describe an optimized workflow for cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement, and data analysis of small
papers.summary: This protocol describes an optimized workflow for preparing small, structurally complex plant tissues for 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics, covering cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement on capture slides, and downstream data analysis. It addresses the practical bottlenecks of rapid preservation, precise orientation, and accurate positioning within the limited capture area, making spatial transcriptomics more accessible for plant developmental studies.

papers.title: Marker-Centered Evaluation of De Novo Assemblers Using Validated Microsatellite Loci in the Endangered Korean Fish Pseudopungtungia nigra.
papers.abstract: The recovery of experimentally validated microsatellite loci from short-read assemblies may provide an application-specific measure of assembly quality that complements conventional genome-wide statistics. In this study, four de novo assemblers-SPAdes, ABySS, SOAPdenovo2, and MaSuRCA-were evaluated using genomic reads from two individuals of the endangered Korean freshwater fish Pseudopungtungia nigra. Assembler performance was assessed based on assembly contiguity, BUSCO completeness, computational requirements, and the recovery of 20 PCR-validated microsatellite loci and their flanking regio
papers.summary: The study benchmarks four de novo assemblers (SPAdes, ABySS, SOAPdenovo2, MaSuRCA) on short-read data from the endangered Korean fish Pseudopungtungia nigra, using both standard metrics (contiguity, BUSCO completeness, computational cost) and a novel marker-centered metric: recovery of 20 PCR-validated microsatellite loci and their flanking regions. This approach provides an application-specific measure of assembly quality that complements genome-wide statistics, showing that assemblers can differ in their ability to recover functionally validated loci even when overall assembly metrics are similar.

papers.title: Synthetic Reconstruction and Characterization of Endogenous Bacteriophage Genomes from Desulfovibrio vulgaris.
papers.abstract: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) caused by sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) is a major challenge in industrial infrastructure, yet the limited availability of well-characterized bacteriophages has hindered the development of phage-based strategies for controlling these organisms. Here, we present an integrated genome-guided workflow for the discovery, validation, and synthetic reconstruction of endogenous prophages from the model sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough. Bioinformatic analysis using PHASTEST identified seven prophage-like regions distributed t
papers.summary: The authors developed a genome-guided workflow to identify, validate, and synthetically reconstruct endogenous prophages from the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, which is implicated in microbiologically influenced corrosion. Bioinformatic analysis revealed seven prophage-like regions, and the study demonstrates a pipeline for reviving these phages, potentially enabling phage-based control strategies for corrosive biofilms.

papers.title: Identification of Genes Associated with Gut Microbiota Metabolites in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Complicated by Acute Cerebral Infarction Based on Bioinformatics and Mendelian Randomization.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and acute cerebral infarction (ACI) are globally prevalent diseases that impose substantial public health burdens. While gut microbiota (GM) is increasingly recognized to regulate metabolic and immune homeostasis linked to both diseases, its shared genetically predicted microbial taxa and underlying metabolite-gene regulatory mechanisms in T2DM and ACI remain unclear, highlighting the need for systematic investigation. Accordingly, this study aimed to elucidate their regulatory mechanisms. Methods: Transcriptomic datasets, genome-wide association stu
papers.summary: This study combined transcriptomic data with Mendelian randomization to identify gut microbiota taxa and metabolites genetically linked to both type 2 diabetes and acute cerebral infarction, then pinpointed candidate genes mediating these metabolite-disease relationships. The work proposes shared microbial-metabolite-gene regulatory axes that may underlie the co-occurrence of these two conditions.

papers.title: Re-Analysis on GRCh38 with the MANE Select Transcript Resolves Previously Undetected Biallelic ODAD4 Variants in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
papers.abstract: Molecular diagnosis is highly sensitive to the human genome assembly used in a bioinformatics pipeline. Panels designed on GRCh37 (hg19) inherit its exon annotation, whereas transcript standards and interpretation databases are anchored to GRCh38 (hg38); a coding exon absent from GRCh37 can therefore be neither targeted nor analyzed. We describe two unrelated individuals with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) in whom first-line, GRCh37-based panel sequencing was non-diagnostic. Both were re-analyzed on GRCh38 against the Matched Annotation from NCBI and EMBL-EBI (MANE) Select transcript. In Pat
papers.summary: Two unrelated patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) remained undiagnosed after standard GRCh37-based panel sequencing. Re-analysis of their data on GRCh38 using the MANE Select transcript revealed biallelic ODAD4 variants that had been missed because a coding exon present in GRCh38 is absent from GRCh37. The study shows that genome assembly and transcript annotation choices can directly determine whether disease-causing variants are detected.

papers.title: Deep Genomic Characterization of Bacillus subtilis SNUY1 & 168 Using MAYA (Multistage Analysis of Prokaryotic Annotations): An Integrated Snakemake-Based Bioinformatics Pipeline.
papers.abstract: Bacillus subtilis is an extensively characterized Gram-positive bacterium with broad applications in agriculture, biotechnology, and biocontrol. Strain SNUY1, known for its antifungal properties and use as an edible coating, has been completely sequenced and deposited in NCBI (accession: CP199918), making it an important model for genomic and functional characterization. Here, we present the MAYA pipeline, a fully automated, rule-based Snakemake workflow that integrates eighteen bioinformatic tools into a single end-to-end framework. MAYA accepts either raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads or p
papers.summary: The authors present MAYA, an automated Snakemake-based pipeline that integrates eighteen bioinformatic tools to perform end-to-end genomic annotation of prokaryotes, accepting either raw Illumina reads or assembled genomes. They apply it to characterize Bacillus subtilis strains SNUY1 and 168, demonstrating a reproducible workflow for functional and comparative genomic analysis. The work is primarily a tooling contribution rather than a novel biological discovery.

papers.title: A step forward in comprehensive nanopore-based forensic profiling of STRs, InDel, SNP and mtDNA for identity and appearance prediction.
papers.abstract: The targeted analysis of diverse DNA markers, including single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), insertion deletion polymorphisms (InDels) and DNA methylation levels, is central to forensic DNA phenotyping, enabling inference of BGA, appearance traits, and age. Such information is relevant when DNA comparison after conventional DNA profiling fails to identify a person of interest. Recent technological developments allow both genetic and epigenetic markers to be analyzed in long-reads within a single platform such as Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT). This approach offers an advantage over trad
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing can simultaneously profile multiple forensic DNA markers—STRs, InDels, SNPs, and mtDNA—along with DNA methylation, enabling both identity matching and appearance/ancestry/age prediction from a single platform. The approach offers an integrated alternative to conventional capillary electrophoresis-based forensic profiling, which typically analyzes only one marker type at a time.

papers.title: Nanopore Sequencing for Epigenetic Decoding: Applications, Analytical Constraints, and Translational Prospects.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation involves multiple molecular layers, including DNA and RNA modifications, histone post-translational modifications (PTMs), and chromatin accessibility. These processes contribute to cell identity, development, and disease, but their measurement remains technically challenging because sequence context, molecular modification, chromatin state, and transcript structure are often assayed separately. As a representative third-generation sequencing technology, nanopore sequencing is profoundly reshaping the interpretation of the epigenetic code through its distinctive capabiliti
papers.summary: This review examines how nanopore sequencing can decode multiple epigenetic layers—DNA and RNA modifications, histone modifications, and chromatin accessibility—from long-read data, potentially integrating what is usually assayed separately. It discusses analytical constraints and translational prospects for using nanopore-based epigenetics in research and clinical settings.

papers.title: Cell-free DNA fragmentomics and epigenomic profiling in hematologic malignancies: current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Mutation-based liquid biopsy supports diagnosis and disease monitoring in hematologic malignancies, but interpretation of plasma variants may be complicated by clonal hematopoiesis, treatment-related changes, and nonmalignant blood-cell turnover. This structured narrative review evaluates whether cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) provide complementary information beyond mutation detection. Direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, although most studies remain retrospective, internally validat
papers.summary: This review examines whether cell-free DNA fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5hmC profiling add useful information beyond mutation-based liquid biopsy in hematologic malignancies, where plasma variant interpretation is complicated by clonal hematopoiesis and treatment-related changes. The authors find that direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, but most studies remain retrospective and internally validated, limiting translation.

papers.title: AI-Assisted WES Variant Interpretation in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Narrative Review of Existing Tools.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of conditions characterized by alterations in brain development and function, frequently associated with complex genetic architectures. The widespread implementation of next-generation sequencing, particularly whole-exome sequencing (WES), has substantially increased the identification of potentially disease-associated variants, shifting the major challenge from variant detection to their interpretation and prioritization. This review examines the emerging contribution of artificial intelligence (AI) to W
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys how artificial intelligence tools are being applied to interpret whole-exome sequencing variants in neurodevelopmental disorders, where the bottleneck has shifted from variant detection to prioritization and interpretation. It catalogs existing AI-assisted approaches and discusses their emerging role in clinical genomics workflows.

papers.title: "A human CHRNA6 3' UTR variant alters the molecular environment and microRNA engagement of the adolescent VTA without changing Chrna6 transcript abundance".
papers.abstract: A single nucleotide polymorphism (rs2304297) in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) of CHRNA6 , encoding the α6 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit, is associated with adolescent smoking behavior. Humanized rats carrying the "C" or "G" allele show sex- and genotype-dependent responses to adolescent nicotine, yet the variant does not alter the protein sequence and the mechanism has remained unknown. We examined the molecular consequences of rs2304297 in vivo in the adolescent ventral tegmental area (VTA). Chrna6 transcript abundance did not differ by genotype, nor did transcript stability or
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how a common non-coding variant (rs2304297) in the 3' UTR of the CHRNA6 gene, linked to adolescent smoking, exerts its effects. Using humanized rats, the authors show that the variant does not change Chrna6 transcript levels or stability in the adolescent ventral tegmental area, but instead alters the local molecular environment and microRNA binding, providing a mechanistic explanation for allele-specific nicotine responses.

papers.title: Clinical and Genetic Characterization of a Family with Tooth Agenesis Carrying a Novel LEF1 Variant.
papers.abstract: Background: Tooth agenesis is one of the most common developmental anomalies of the human dentition and may occur either as an isolated trait or as part of a syndromic condition. Advances in genomic technologies have facilitated the identification of genes involved in odontogenesis, including LEF1 (Lymphoid Enhancer-Binding Factor 1), a key transcription factor in the WNT signaling pathway. Methods: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed in a proband with non-syndromic tooth agenesis to investigate the underlying genetic cause. Parental segregation analysis was performed through Sanger seq
papers.summary: This case report describes a family with non-syndromic tooth agenesis in which whole-exome sequencing identified a novel variant in LEF1, a WNT-pathway transcription factor involved in tooth development. Sanger sequencing confirmed segregation of the variant with the phenotype in the family. The finding adds to the growing list of LEF1 variants associated with inherited tooth agenesis.

papers.title: Structural and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Human β-Defensin 1 Variants Reveals Distinct Perturbation Signatures.
papers.abstract: Human β-defensin 1 (hBD-1) is a small, disulfide-constrained antimicrobial peptide produced predominantly in the kidney and urogenital tract, where it contributes to epithelial innate defense. Genetic variation in the gene encoding hBD-1 has been associated with altered expression levels and susceptibility to infections, including infection following solid organ transplantation, yet the molecular consequences of coding substitutions in the active, mature form remain largely undefined. Here, we integrate conventional genomics, protein bioinformatics, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations to examine how naturally occurring genetic variants in the mature human β-defensin 1 antimicrobial peptide affect its structure and dynamics. The authors identify distinct perturbation signatures for different variants, suggesting that coding substitutions can alter the peptide's biophysical behavior in ways that may relate to infection susceptibility. The work links genomic variation to molecular-level structural consequences for an innate immune peptide.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of incomplete penetrance in 4,325 rare disease families reveals divergent transcriptional networks in CHD8 pathology.
papers.abstract: Despite major advances in genomic sequencing and analytical pipelines for rare disorders, more than 50% of affected individuals remain without a molecular diagnosis. One challenge is the interpretation of inherited variants exhibiting incomplete penetrance (IP).
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates incomplete penetrance in 4,325 rare disease families, aiming to improve interpretation of inherited variants that do not always cause disease. Focusing on CHD8 pathology, the authors identify divergent transcriptional networks associated with penetrance, suggesting that network-level effects help explain why some carriers remain unaffected.

papers.title: Beyond molecular snapshots: Regulatory trajectories in dynamic epigenetic regulation.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation is commonly interpreted through molecular markers measured at discrete timepoints. While such approaches have generated important biological insights, they primarily provide static representations of regulatory states and may therefore capture only a limited component of dynamic biological processes. Emerging evidence from chromatin biology, transcriptional regulation and genome organisation suggests that biological regulation unfolds through continuously evolving interactions across multiple molecular layers. This article presents a biological hypothesis and conceptual f
papers.summary: This conceptual paper argues that epigenetic regulation is inherently dynamic and cannot be fully understood from static molecular snapshots at discrete timepoints. The authors propose a hypothesis that regulation unfolds through continuously evolving interactions across multiple molecular layers, including chromatin, transcription, and genome organization. The work is a perspective piece rather than an empirical study, aiming to reframe how dynamic epigenetic regulation should be conceptualized and studied.

papers.title: Overcoming a diagnostic blindspot: Identifying balanced translocations in Mendelian rare disease cohorts.
papers.abstract: Short-read genome sequencing generates the signal necessary to detect balanced reciprocal translocations at single-nucleotide resolution, but standard structural variant callers represent them as breakend pairs. Structural variant callers produce thousands of breakend records per genome, the majority of which are false positives arising from segmental duplications, repetitive elements, and reference assembly artifacts. This specificity problem has prevented balanced translocation detection from entering routine genome sequencing workflows. We developed a highly specific pipeline to resolve bal
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors developed a highly specific pipeline to detect balanced reciprocal translocations from short-read genome sequencing data, addressing the problem that standard structural variant callers produce thousands of false-positive breakend records. This enables balanced translocation detection to enter routine genome sequencing workflows for Mendelian rare disease cohorts, overcoming a diagnostic blindspot.

papers.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug pert
papers.summary: This study compared primary breast tumor transcriptomes from patients with and without circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in their blood, using RNA-seq and bioinformatics analyses. It identified gene expression signatures that distinguish CTC-negative from CTC-positive states, revealing a progression from early remodeling programs to metastatic-associated gene expression. The work also linked these signatures to survival outcomes and potential drug targets.

papers.title: Whole-Genome Sequencing Reveals the Resistome, Virulome, Pan-Genome Architecture, and Phylogenomic Diversity of Extensively Drug-Resistant Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhi in Pakistan.
papers.abstract: The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi has severely constrained typhoid treatment. Pakistan is a major hotspot for XDR typhoid, yet genomic evidence defining the molecular basis of antimicrobial resistance, virulence, and genomic diversity of circulating strains remains limited. A cross-sectional study was conducted from January to December 2021 involving 252 culture-confirmed S. Typhi isolates collected from patients with suspected typhoid fever in Peshawar, Pakistan. Isolates were identified by conventional microbiolo
papers.summary: This study performed whole-genome sequencing on 252 Salmonella Typhi isolates from Peshawar, Pakistan, to characterize the resistome, virulome, pan-genome, and phylogenomic diversity of extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains. The genomic analysis reveals the molecular basis of antimicrobial resistance and virulence in circulating XDR typhoid strains, providing much-needed genomic surveillance data from a major XDR hotspot. The findings help define the genetic architecture underlying the ongoing XDR typhoid outbreak in Pakistan.

papers.title: Ryder: epigenome normalization using a two-tier model and internal reference regions.
papers.abstract: Sequencing-based epigenomic profiling methods are powerful but suffer from technical variability that complicates cross-sample comparisons and can obscure true biological signals. While existing normalization methods using spike-in controls or computational approaches have been proposed, they often rely on assumptions that may not hold across diverse experimental conditions or require additional data types.
papers.summary: Ryder introduces a two-tier normalization model for sequencing-based epigenomic data that uses internal reference regions instead of spike-in controls, aiming to correct technical variability across samples without requiring additional data types. This approach addresses limitations of existing spike-in and computational normalization methods that rely on assumptions that may not hold across diverse experimental conditions.

papers.title: HINN prioritizes multi-omics biomarkers associated with cognitive decline.
papers.abstract: Integrating multi-omics data for disease prediction remains challenging due to the complexity of cross-layer biological interactions and the limited use of prior biological knowledge in many machine learning models. We present the Hierarchical Input Neural Network (HINN), a deep learning framework that incorporates biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships in a structured and interpretable manner. HINN was applied to blood-derived multi-omics data to predict cognitive assessment scores, including Mini-Mental State
papers.summary: HINN is a deep learning framework that uses biologically informed connections between genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships in a structured, interpretable way. Applied to blood-derived multi-omics data, it predicts cognitive assessment scores such as the Mini-Mental State Examination and prioritizes biomarkers associated with cognitive decline. The approach improves interpretability over standard machine learning models by incorporating prior biological knowledge into the network architecture.

papers.title: A clinical case of X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia caused by an Xq13.1 duplication affecting the EDA gene.
papers.abstract: X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia (XLHED; Christ-Siemens-Touraine syndrome, ICD-10: Q82.4) is the most common type of ectodermal dysplasia, caused by genetic disorders of ectodermal derivatives. The condition significantly impacts patients' quality of life, presenting with a classic triad of hypohidrosis, hypotrichosis and hypodontia, which creates a risk of impaired thermoregulation and necessitates complex dental rehabilitation. The molecular basis of the disease lies in alterations of the EDA gene, which encodes ectodysplasin A. This protein belongs to the tumor necrosis factor (TN
papers.summary: This clinical case report describes a patient with X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia (XLHED), characterized by the classic triad of reduced sweating, sparse hair, and missing teeth, caused by an Xq13.1 duplication encompassing the EDA gene. The finding adds a structural copy-number variant to the spectrum of EDA mutations underlying this disorder and underscores the importance of detecting duplications in molecular diagnostics.

papers.title: Analytical and clinical validation of the EdenDx methylation assay as a noninvasive supportive triage tool for early detection of endometrial cancer in cervical scraping specimens.
papers.abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) is the most common gynecologic malignancy; however, early detection remains challenging due to overlapping symptoms and the absence of validated noninvasive triage testing. Diagnosis relies on invasive procedures such as endometrial biopsy or dilation and curettage. The EdenDx assay detects hypermethylation of CDO1 and CELF4 genes, which are specifically associated with EC and have been shown to be epigenetically altered prior to symptom onset. Here, we evaluate the clinical and analytical performance of the EdenDx assay as a noninvasive triage tool for the early detect
papers.summary: This study validates the EdenDx assay, which detects hypermethylation of the CDO1 and CELF4 genes in cervical scraping specimens, as a noninvasive triage tool for early detection of endometrial cancer. The assay aims to reduce reliance on invasive endometrial biopsy or dilation and curettage by identifying epigenetic changes that occur before symptom onset. Analytical and clinical performance metrics are reported to support its use in early detection workflows.

papers.title: A Guide to Enzymatic Targeted Methylation Sequencing Bioinformatics Workflow: Best Practices.
papers.abstract: We present a best-practices protocol for targeted DNA methylation sequencing analysis that integrates both bisulfite- and enzymatic-conversion approaches using Twist Bioscience technology. Building on established tools and vendor-recommended workflows, this protocol provides a standardized, fully reproducible framework that addresses current gaps in the implementation, documentation, and downstream integration of targeted methylation sequencing analyses. The workflow incorporates widely used open-source tools across two main stages: preprocessing (adapter trimming with Trim Galore and quality
papers.summary: This protocol provides a standardized, reproducible bioinformatics workflow for analyzing targeted DNA methylation sequencing data generated by both bisulfite and enzymatic conversion methods using Twist Bioscience technology. It integrates widely used open-source tools across preprocessing and downstream analysis stages, addressing gaps in implementation and documentation. The guide aims to help researchers consistently process and interpret targeted methylation data.

papers.title: Epigenetics in cancer: from mechanisms to precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Epigenetics encompasses heritable yet reversible changes in gene expression that occur without alterations to the underlying DNA sequence. Through coordinated regulation of DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and higher-order chromatin organization, epigenetic mechanisms shape chromatin accessibility and transcriptional programs that govern cellular identity, plasticity, and tissue homeostasis. In cancer, disruption of the epigenetic landscape has emerged as a hallmark of tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. Unlike gen
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how epigenetic mechanisms—DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and higher-order chromatin organization—are disrupted in cancer and contribute to tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and therapy resistance. It argues that because epigenetic changes are reversible, they offer promising targets for precision medicine approaches, including epigenetic therapies and biomarkers.

papers.title: DeCTCF: Decoding CTCF binding sequences by leveraging predicted epigenomic features.
papers.abstract: CTCF is a key architectural protein with diverse roles in genome organization and gene regulation, yet how it achieves these roles in different contexts remains unclear. Pretrained sequence-based models such as Sei provide predicted epigenomic features that can be used in downstream analyses of regulatory elements. Here, we developed DeCTCF, an integrative computational framework that uses pretrained Sei predictions to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences by integrating CTCF ChIP-seq data from 118 human cell lines. By leveraging predicted epigenomic features from the Sei model, we grouped th
papers.summary: DeCTCF is a computational framework that uses predicted epigenomic features from the pretrained Sei model to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences across 118 human cell lines. By integrating these predictions with CTCF ChIP-seq data, the authors group binding sites into distinct clusters, revealing how CTCF's diverse regulatory roles may be context-dependent. This provides a new way to decode CTCF binding sequences without relying solely on experimental epigenomic data.

papers.title: Clinical Epigenomics in Rare Diseases: Interpreting DNA Methylation Episignatures.
papers.abstract: Epigenomic testing complements sequence-based analysis by detecting downstream changes in epigenomic state associated with genetic variation. Genome-wide DNA methylation episignatures are reproducible molecular phenotypes that can serve as biomarkers of specific Mendelian disorders, particularly those involving chromatin regulators, DNA methylation machinery, and transcriptional regulatory pathways.
papers.summary: This paper reviews how genome-wide DNA methylation episignatures—reproducible patterns of methylation change—can serve as clinical biomarkers for rare Mendelian disorders, especially those caused by mutations in chromatin regulators and DNA methylation machinery. It discusses how epigenomic testing complements standard sequence-based diagnostics by capturing downstream functional consequences of genetic variants, aiding interpretation and diagnosis.

papers.title: Establishment of Uveal Melanoma Patient-Derived Organoids Using an Air-Liquid Interface System for Translational Research.
papers.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, with a unique genetic and epigenetic profile and a high metastatic risk. The lack of experimental models to replicate tumor biology, including its epigenetic landscape, limits progress in translational research. Recently, patient-derived organoid (PDO) models have emerged as a promising tool for the modeling of various tumors, including UM. This study aims to establish an air-liquid interface (ALI) PDO culture system for UM, evaluate its similarity to the primary tumors, and assess its utility for drug screening.
papers.summary: This study establishes patient-derived organoid models of uveal melanoma using an air-liquid interface culture system, aiming to better replicate the tumor's genetic and epigenetic landscape than existing models. The authors evaluate how closely these organoids resemble primary tumors and test their use for drug screening, addressing a key gap in translational research for this aggressive intraocular cancer.

papers.title: Deep Learning Predicts Hematopoietic Stem Cell Aging From 3D Chromatin Images.
papers.abstract: The functional decline of the hematopoietic system during aging affects organismal function and contributes to reduced healthspan. Quantifying hematopoietic aging holds great scientific and clinical relevance. Alterations in chromatin architecture are a well-established hallmark of aging that encode rich and informative signatures of the aging process, yet they remain largely unexplored as quantitative markers. Here, we present an interpretable deep learning approach based on convolutional neural networks, ChromAgeNet, that learns changes in the spatial features of chromatin architecture upon
papers.summary: The authors developed ChromAgeNet, a convolutional neural network that predicts hematopoietic stem cell aging from 3D chromatin images. The model learns spatial chromatin features that change with age, providing an interpretable quantitative marker of aging. This demonstrates that chromatin architecture can serve as a rich, informative signature of the aging process.

papers.title: Investigation of allele-specific expression in citrus hybrids reveals the association between siRNA-mediated de novo methylation and high expression in citrus genomes.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation plays a central role in the regulation of gene expression. In plants, methylation occurs in the CG, CHG, and CHH contexts, via distinct DNA methyltransferases including MET1, CMT3, and the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway via DRM2. In interspecific hybrids, these epigenetic mechanisms are confronted to a mixed small RNA population and two subgenomes harbouring specific methylation patterns, therefore generating unique expression profiles. The aim of this work was to understand these regulations by analysing gene expression, DNA methylation, and small RNAs in a citrus
papers.summary: This study examines allele-specific expression in citrus interspecific hybrids, integrating gene expression, DNA methylation, and small RNA data to understand how epigenetic regulation differs between parental subgenomes. The authors report an association between siRNA-mediated de novo methylation and high gene expression in citrus genomes, suggesting that RdDM-linked methylation can correlate with elevated transcription rather than silencing. The work highlights how mixed small RNA populations in hybrids generate unique expression and methylation profiles.

papers.title: "Updates on diagnostic and prognostic molecular biomarkers of CNS tumors".
papers.abstract: The diagnosis and classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors has undergone a paradigm shift over the past decade, evolving from a purely histology-based approach to an integrated framework that incorporates molecular and epigenetic features. This review summarizes recent updates in key genomic and epigenomic biomarkers across major CNS tumor categories, with a focus on their diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications. DNA methylation profiling has emerged as a valuable tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, complementing traditional histopathologic assess
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in molecular and epigenetic biomarkers used to diagnose and classify central nervous system tumors. It highlights how DNA methylation profiling, alongside genomic markers, now complements traditional histology to improve tumor classification, subgrouping, grading, and prognostication across major CNS tumor categories.

papers.title: A patient-derived missense mouse model of Kabuki syndrome 1.
papers.abstract: Kabuki syndrome type 1 (KS1) is a rare cause of intellectual disability resulting from heterozygous pathogenic variants in the gene encoding the histone methyltransferase KMT2D. A previously established loss-of-function mouse model of KS1 exhibits key phenotypic features, and therapeutic trials in this mouse model suggest postnatal malleability of neurological symptoms. However, 15-30% of individuals with KS1 carry missense variants. To investigate whether missense variants lead to similar phenotypic presentation in mice, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to introduce the KS1 patient variant R5179H, corresp
papers.summary: This study used CRISPR-Cas9 to create a mouse model carrying the patient-derived missense variant R5179H in KMT2D, the gene mutated in Kabuki syndrome type 1. Since 15-30% of KS1 patients have missense variants rather than loss-of-function mutations, this model tests whether missense variants produce comparable phenotypes. The work provides a new tool for studying the subset of KS1 caused by missense mutations and for evaluating whether findings from loss-of-function models generalize.

papers.title: Multiscale modeling primer: Focus on chromatin and epigenetics.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in modern biology is to understand how molecular interactions produce cellular and organismal functions across vast spatiotemporal scales. Nowhere is this challenge more apparent than in the study of chromatin, where meters of DNA compact into a micron-sized nucleus. How this polymer folds is a dynamic process, regulated by epigenetic modifications-chemical changes to DNA and histones that involve only a handful of atoms. These small changes cooperate to produce emergent, higher-order structures that define cellular identity and function. To explain this system, we must int
papers.summary: This primer reviews multiscale modeling approaches for understanding how chromatin folds and functions across spatiotemporal scales, from atomic-level epigenetic modifications to micron-scale nuclear organization. It explains how small chemical changes to DNA and histones cooperate to produce emergent higher-order chromatin structures that define cellular identity. The article serves as an introductory guide to integrating computational models spanning molecular to cellular scales in epigenetics research.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial biology approaches, particularly spatial transcriptomics, are being applied to cancer epigenetics to study how local tissue context influences regulatory programs in tumors. It highlights that while bulk and single-cell sequencing have advanced tumor biology understanding, they lose spatial information, and spatial methods now reveal tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-cell communication. The abstract is truncated but appears to argue for integrating spatial context into epigenetic cancer research.

papers.title: A Pan-Methylome Framework for Population-Scale Bacterial Epigenomics.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic modifications furnish a hidden regulatory layer that shapes cellular fate and evolutionary potential without rewriting the genetic code. In eukaryotes, methylome maps have profoundly transformed our understanding of development, disease, and lineage diversification. In bacteria, which represent the most abundant and ecologically versatile forms of life, the epigenome remains a largely uncharted dimension. To enable population-scale comparison of bacterial methylomes, we develop a principled strategy to prioritize methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded, broadly conserved
papers.summary: The authors present a framework for population-scale bacterial epigenomics that prioritizes methylation systems which are enzymatically encoded and broadly conserved, enabling systematic comparison of methylomes across bacterial populations. This addresses the current gap in bacterial epigenome mapping, where methylome data remain sparse compared to eukaryotes, and provides a principled strategy for selecting which methylation systems to profile at scale.

papers.title: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling: Technologies, computation, and applications in precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Cancer is an intrinsically heterogeneous disease characterized by distinct malignant subclones defined by specific genetic and epigenetic alterations, such as aberrant DNA methylation. Traditional bulk sequencing methods analyze large populations of cells in aggregate, yielding an averaged methylome signal that masks the rare but clinically significant epigenetic patterns driving tumor initiation, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. The emergence of single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAme) sequencing has driven a paradigm shift in oncology by providing the resolution required to dissect this
papers.summary: This review surveys single-cell DNA methylation sequencing technologies, computational methods, and applications in precision oncology. It argues that scDNAme resolves epigenetic heterogeneity masked by bulk sequencing, enabling detection of rare malignant subclones and methylation patterns linked to tumor initiation, metastasis, and therapy resistance.

papers.title: Epigenetics and In Silico Transcriptome Analysis of Pediatric Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
papers.abstract: Pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous hematologic malignancy that accounts for about 15%-20% of childhood leukemias. Despite therapeutic advances, relapses remain common, and survival for high-risk patients is below 60%. Unlike adult AML, pediatric AML displays distinct genetic mutations, including FLT3-ITD, NPM1, KMT2A rearrangements, and core-binding factors (CBF) fusions, as well as extensive epigenetic dysregulation. Aberrant DNA methylation, histone modifications, and altered non-coding RNA expressions disrupt hematopoietic differentiation and activate oncogenic transc
papers.summary: This review examines the epigenetic landscape of pediatric acute myeloid leukemia, focusing on how aberrant DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNA dysregulation contribute to disease pathogenesis alongside characteristic mutations like FLT3-ITD, NPM1, and KMT2A rearrangements. The authors also discuss in silico transcriptome analysis approaches for identifying epigenetic drivers and potential therapeutic targets in this heterogeneous childhood malignancy.

papers.title: A machine learning classifier reveals hidden rare biallelic heterozygous variants in the coding regions of Meniere disease genome.
papers.abstract: Meniere disease (MD) is a rare inner ear disorder with a significant genetic contribution. We developed the MD classifier, an ML tool to distinguish familial from sporadic MD cases using rare variants in coding regions. We have generated a disease-specific gene variant score incorporating gene, variant, and disease-specific features. A gradient boosting classifier achieved the highest performance, with a test AUC of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.702-0.948) and an accuracy of 81.5%. Reclassification of sporadic cases into the familial group ranged from 16.6% to 28.3%. The model identified a burden of bialle
papers.summary: The authors built a machine learning classifier (gradient boosting) that uses rare coding-region variants to distinguish familial from sporadic Meniere disease cases, achieving a test AUC of 0.843 and 81.5% accuracy. Reclassifying sporadic cases as familial (16.6–28.3%) revealed a hidden burden of biallelic heterozygous variants, suggesting some sporadic cases may actually have a genetic basis.

papers.title: Diverse patterns of transcriptional regulation and epigenetic reprogramming within PMDs contribute to ESCC progression by regulating EMT and immunosuppression.
papers.abstract: Partially methylated domains (PMDs) represent extensive genome-wide hypomethylated regions that drive genomic instability and proto-oncogene activation. However, their complex regulatory influence on tumor-specific transcriptional networks remains largely elusive. In this study, we developed a robust computational pipeline to characterize aberrant PMD landscapes across pan-cancer. We specifically focused on the epigenetic features associated with transcriptional dysregulation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). By analyzing gene expression patterns, we classified PMDs into four disti
papers.summary: The study develops a computational pipeline to map partially methylated domains (PMDs) across cancers and applies it to esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). It classifies PMDs into four distinct subtypes based on gene expression patterns, showing that different PMD classes regulate epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and immunosuppression, contributing to tumor progression. This reveals that PMDs are not uniform but have diverse regulatory roles in shaping cancer transcriptional networks.

papers.title: Controlling for DNA dosage with whole-genome sequencing improves ATAC-seq peak calling.
papers.abstract: ATAC-seq is a powerful method for mapping chromatin accessibility and identifying cis-regulatory elements (CREs) across cell types. We reveal that ATAC-seq peak calling is compromised by local biases in DNA dosage, arising from copy number variations but also from DNA replication timing. As part of the FANTOM consortium's efforts, we propose enhancing the model-based analysis of ChIP-seq pipeline by integrating whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data, analogous to input controls in ChIP-seq analyses. This adjustment increases both the number and width of ATAC peaks, with improved proximity to trans
papers.summary: ATAC-seq peak calling is biased by local variation in DNA copy number and replication timing, which can create false or distorted accessibility signals. The authors show that incorporating whole-genome sequencing data as an input control, analogous to ChIP-seq input controls, corrects for these DNA dosage biases and yields more and wider ATAC peaks that better align with regulatory elements. This provides a simple methodological improvement for chromatin accessibility studies.

papers.title: Strategic roadmap for FAIR-compliant transcriptomic workflows: from technical challenges to bioinformatics democratization.
papers.abstract: This article draws on the authors' more than 17 years of experience in transcriptomic research, beginning with the introduction of high-throughput sequencing in Mexico in 2009. Here, we provide a critical review of bioinformatics pipelines for different RNA classes, ranging from small RNAs to long non-coding RNAs. Our analysis encompasses a range of scenarios, from de novo transcriptome assembly for organisms lacking a closely related and adequately annotated reference genome to differential expression analysis based on a well-annotated reference genome. By providing a comprehensive overview o
papers.summary: This review distills 17+ years of transcriptomic research experience into a critical assessment of bioinformatics pipelines for diverse RNA classes, from small RNAs to long non-coding RNAs. It covers scenarios ranging from de novo transcriptome assembly for poorly annotated organisms to differential expression analysis with well-annotated references, and argues for FAIR-compliant workflows that democratize bioinformatics access. The paper serves as a practical roadmap for researchers, particularly in resource-limited settings, navigating technical and infrastructural challenges in transcriptomic analysis.

papers.title: gTranslate: rapid and accurate translation table prediction for prokaryotic genomes.
papers.abstract: Bioinformatic tools often require the prediction of protein-coding genes to make inferences about prokaryotic genomes. Typically, the genetic code used for translating genes to proteins must be specified by the user based on the taxonomic classification of a genome assembly or, for some widely used tools, established using a heuristic rule based on gene coding densities. Manual specification is at best inconvenient, but more challenging is that many bioinformatic tools are applied before taxonomic classifications have been established making specifying the translation table impractical.
papers.summary: gTranslate is a new tool that predicts the correct genetic code (translation table) for prokaryotic genomes directly from sequence data, without requiring prior taxonomic classification. This addresses a common bottleneck where users must manually specify the translation table or rely on heuristic rules based on gene coding density. The tool aims to make gene prediction and downstream bioinformatic analyses faster and more accurate.

papers.title: PoLoCo: a reproducible pooled low-coverage workflow for draft genome assembly and allele frequency analysis from ethanol-preserved small non-model invertebrates.
papers.abstract: Many ecologically important small invertebrates are preserved in ethanol, which compromises DNA integrity and severely limits their potential to be utilized in further genomic research. The lack of soil arthropod representation ultimately results in limited availability of reference genomes and population genomic inference from pooled sequencing (Pool-seq).
papers.summary: PoLoCo is a reproducible workflow for generating draft genome assemblies and allele frequency estimates from pooled, low-coverage sequencing of small non-model invertebrates preserved in ethanol. It addresses the challenge of degraded DNA in ethanol-preserved soil arthropods, a group with poor genomic representation, enabling population genomic inference where reference genomes are scarce.

papers.title: Discovery and annotation of putative genes and novel RNA splice-isoforms in the human heart.
papers.abstract: The analysis of long-read RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data can extend current annotations across the genomes, transcriptomes, and proteomes of even the most annotated species such as Homo sapiens. Long-read sequencing (LRS) technologies like Oxford Nanopore Technologies' (ONTs) nanopore sequencing can capture full-length transcripts, making the task of read-to-isoform assignment less challenging. This enables both the discovery of new RNA splice isoforms as well as a more accurate measure of their individual expression. RNA expression from unannotated regions of the genome can also lead to the di
papers.summary: This study uses long-read Oxford Nanopore RNA sequencing to discover and annotate previously uncharacterized genes and novel RNA splice isoforms in human heart tissue. By capturing full-length transcripts, the authors improve read-to-isoform assignment and quantify expression of newly identified isoforms, including those from unannotated genomic regions. The work expands the human heart transcriptome annotation and provides a resource for studying cardiac gene expression.

papers.title: TorchGWAS 1.0: GPU-accelerated GWAS at scale.
papers.abstract: Imaging, molecular and machine-learning workflows can generate thousands of quantitative phenotypes in one cohort. Repeating genome-wide scans trait by trait creates a computational and output bottleneck.
papers.summary: TorchGWAS 1.0 is a GPU-accelerated tool for running genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across thousands of quantitative traits simultaneously, addressing the computational and output bottleneck of trait-by-trait scanning. It leverages GPU parallelism to make large-scale phenome-wide association feasible for cohorts with imaging, molecular, or machine-learning-derived phenotypes.

papers.title: OBLX: building standardized reference resources for reproducible bioinformatics data analysis.
papers.abstract: Reproducible next-generation sequencing (NGS) analyses in cancer research require standardized reference genome resources, yet these resources are often assembled inconsistently, limiting the comparability of results across pipelines and studies. While existing solutions support a range of workflows, they provide only limited documentation of the included data and processing steps. Furthermore, some of these resources are not version-matched or outdated, making them less suitable for integrated and reproducible cancer genomics analyses. To address this gap, we developed the Omics builder for B
papers.summary: OBLX is a tool for building standardized reference genome resources for reproducible NGS analysis in cancer research. It addresses the problem of inconsistent reference assembly and poor documentation by providing version-matched, well-documented resources. This improves comparability of results across pipelines and studies.

papers.title: The double-edged sword of TOX: orchestrating T cell exhaustion and epigenetic remodeling in the tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: The capacity to profoundly change chromatin domains and in turn drive or inhibit gene expression makes chromatin modulators a powerful tool adopted to regulate crucial steps during development and cell lineage specification. These proteins can however be as well engaged to irreversibly reprogram cells toward pathological outcomes such as cancer. An example of such chromatin remodelers is the family of Thymocyte-selection associated high mobility box proteins (TOX), which has rather pleiotropic functions during development and in cancer. In light of the most recent findings, this review gives a
papers.summary: This review examines the TOX family of chromatin remodelers, which have pleiotropic roles in development and cancer. It focuses on how TOX proteins orchestrate T cell exhaustion and epigenetic remodeling within the tumor microenvironment, highlighting their double-edged nature in both driving and potentially inhibiting pathological outcomes.
